payload.proof_nl:
Let
F(t)=\sum_{g=0}^{\infty} a_g t^g \in \mathbb Z[[t]]

and suppose there exists
C(t)=\sum_{g=0}^{\infty} c_g t^g \in \mathbb Z[[t]]
with each c_g\ge 0 such that
\[(1-t)F(t)=a_0+tC(t).\]
All identities are in the ring of formal power series, so coefficients of equal series are equal termwise.

First expand the left-hand side:
\[
(1-t)F(t)=F(t)-tF(t)
=\sum_{g=0}^{\infty} a_g t^g-\sum_{g=0}^{\infty} a_g t^{g+1}.
\]
Reindex the second sum:
\[
\sum_{g=0}^{\infty} a_g t^{g+1}=\sum_{g=1}^{\infty} a_{g-1} t^g.
\]
Hence
\[
(1-t)F(t)=a_0+\sum_{g=1}^{\infty}(a_g-a_{g-1})t^g.
\]
On the other hand,
\[
a_0+tC(t)=a_0+\sum_{g=0}^{\infty} c_g t^{g+1}=a_0+\sum_{g=1}^{\infty} c_{g-1} t^g.
\]
Since these two formal power series are equal, their coefficients of t^g are equal for every g\ge 1. Therefore
\[
a_g-a_{g-1}=c_{g-1}\qquad (g\ge 1).
\]
Now replace g by g+1. For every integer g\ge 0 we obtain
\[
a_{g+1}-a_g=c_g.
\]
Because each c_g\in \mathbb Z_{\ge 0}, it follows that
\[
a_{g+1}-a_g\ge 0,
\]
so
\[
a_g\le a_{g+1}
\qquad \text{for every } g\ge 0.
\]
This proves both assertions.

payload.statement_nl: Let F(t)=sum_{g=0}^infinity a_g t^g be a formal power series with integer coefficients. Suppose there exists another formal power series C(t)=sum_{g=0}^infinity c_g t^g with all c_g in Z_{>=0} such that (1-t) F(t) = a_0 + t C(t). Then for every integer g >= 0 one has a_{g+1} - a_g = c_g. In particular, a_g <= a_{g+1} for every g >= 0.

detailed_findings.finding: Coefficient extraction from the identity (1-t)F(t)=a_0+tC(t) is carried out correctly in the ring of formal power series.
The reindexing of the shifted series tF(t)=sum_{g=1}^infty a_{g-1} t^g is correct and the resulting coefficient formula is exact.
The conclusion a_{g+1}-a_g=c_g and hence a_g <= a_{g+1} for all g >= 0 matches the stated lemma with no semantic drift.

result_payload.reason: The proof correctly expands the formal power series identity, reindexes the shifted sum, equates coefficients in Z[[t]], and derives a_g - a_{g-1} = c_{g-1} for g >= 1, hence a_{g+1} - a_g = c_g for all g >= 0. Since c_g >= 0, monotonicity follows immediately. The argument is complete and matches the lemma's semantic sketch and its role in the root theorem.
